title: Memory prices and GNG Electronics
thesis: The claim this page tests: memory prices are rising fast, dearer memory makes new PCs dearer, and that widens the room for a refurbisher like GNG. The desk checked the first half on 19 Sep 2026 and traced the second through GNG's own filings, channel by channel, in its report of the same date.

audit.text: Partly holds. The price rise is real, and it has already helped GNG's reported numbers; but memory is also a cost to GNG, the benefit was bought with cash, and the share price ran ahead of the results.
findings: The rise is real and large. TrendForce put first-quarter 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices up 90–95% on the quarter and PC DRAM up more than 100%, a record. The producers' own latest results agree in direction: DRAM selling prices up about 30% on the quarter at SK hynix and in the mid-40s at Samsung for April–June 2026, and in the low-60s at Micron for its quarter to 28 May.

It is decelerating. TrendForce's third-quarter 2026 call for PC DRAM is reported at 15–20%, and its fourth-quarter call at 3–8%. Those are forecasts, and these two reached the desk through secondary reports. The report's reading: a slowdown removes GNG's holding gain on stock bought early, not the price umbrella.

Three channels help GNG and are already in the reported numbers: dearer new PCs, holding gains on inventory bought earlier, and a sales mix shifting to the US and Europe on a weaker rupee. Gross profit per device stepped from about ₹5,000–5,450 to about ₹6,780 in Q1 FY27. That figure is the desk's derivation.

Two channels hurt and arrive late. GNG buys RAM and SSDs to upgrade the machines it refurbishes, and management conceded on its 30 Jul 2026 call that enterprises keeping their fleets longer will shrink the supply of used machines. No document gives memory's share of a refurbished unit's cost.
The benefit was bought with cash. FY26 operating cash flow was −₹215.3 Cr against a reported profit of ₹132.0 Cr, from the annual report's cash flow statement: the trade was placed in inventory.

The share price got there first. It ignored the thesis for four months, to its post-listing low on 27 Jan 2026, and has since run ahead of the results twice. Since GNG listed, its weekly returns have correlated 0.11 with Micron's.

DDR4 is dearer than DDR5 on the spot market: on 18 Sep 2026 a 16Gb DDR4 chip averaged $85.75 against $56.00 for DDR5, as the older standard is wound down. GNG's filed transcript says an entry-level new laptop in India went from ₹40,000 to ₹48,000; a news report of the same call said ₹42,000.

cannot: This is not a price feed. TrendForce's daily quotes are what it sells; this page records figures that it and the producers have published, each with its source, and links to the live page.
Most of the TrendForce figures are forecasts of quarterly contract-price changes, recorded here at the low end of the stated range. The range is in the detail column.
Spot and contract are different markets. Spot is small and volatile; most memory is sold on contract.
A share price is not a memory price. Micron and SK hynix are shown as liquid, daily proxies for the memory cycle, and they also move with everything else that moves semiconductor shares.
What share of a refurbished machine's cost is memory and storage is a question for GNG's disclosures. No price series can answer it.
